purpose: Separate anchor count/content from realized within-Person Rater connectivity, and test whether graph-component anchoring predicts exact conditional-information rank under identical response bytes.

simulation.base_administration: Each non-bridge Person is assigned one Rater and all four Criteria; base Raters are balanced after a seeded Person permutation.
simulation.bridge_administration: Each bridge Person is assigned one frozen Rater edge and receives all four Criteria from both endpoint Raters; no duplicate Person-Rater-Criterion unit occurs.
simulation.same_byte_rule: All five anchor scenarios for a topology-replicate receive identical generated rows in identical order.
simulation.persistence_rule: Write generated responses with %.17g floats, reload with round-trip parsing, and require exact tabular fingerprint.

anchor_scenarios.selection: explicit prospectively frozen level by replicate
explicit prospectively frozen levels by replicate
explicit prospectively frozen levels by replicate

frozen_random_anchor_levels.algorithm: numpy default_rng PCG64 permutation of R01 through R06 once per replicate; first 1, sorted first 2, and sorted first 3

fit_contract.failure_accounting: Every audit and every eligible fit is retained; rank-deficient designs are expected negative controls, not failed optimizer attempts.

realized_graph_contract.informative_person: Observed total is strictly between the minimum and maximum possible total for that Person's administered rows.
realized_graph_contract.edge: Two Rater levels are joined when at least one informative Person has observations from both.
realized_graph_contract.prediction_without_hard_anchors: Rater block is predicted identified only when the realized informative Rater graph is connected; the native sum-to-zero Rater coordinates supply one global origin constraint.
realized_graph_contract.prediction_with_hard_anchors: Rater block is predicted identified only when every realized graph component containing a free Rater also contains at least one hard-anchored Rater.
realized_graph_contract.prediction_scope: Necessary design-level Rater-block prediction; exact conditional rank remains authoritative and can expose additional Criterion/Step or realized-score deficiencies.

frozen_outputs: generated response file and exact round-trip fingerprint
realized informative bridge edges, component membership, and support counts
graph-predicted versus exact conditional eligibility confusion table
conditional rank, nullity, zero-point condition number, issues, work and memory proxies
eligible-fit return, stationarity, fitted-rank, condition-number, and inference-readiness evidence
structural recovery separated by anchored/free status
fit-sample WLE recovery and raw Person Infit/Outfit for inference-ready fits
raw versus three/six-decimal decision disagreements and boundary-distance counts
replicate-level summaries before pooled descriptive summaries
condition-number versus effective bridge-support figure and rank/eligibility heatmap

prospective_expectations_not_success_gat.no_bridge: Any scenario leaving a free Rater is expected rank deficient; all-six-correct removes the Rater block and is expected eligible if Criterion/Step information remains full rank.
prospective_expectations_not_success_gat.two_clusters_strong: Unanchored identification is expected to retain one between-component null direction. Random anchors are expected to restore Rater-block identification only when both realized components are covered, while all-six-correct removes the block.
prospective_expectations_not_success_gat.connected_topologies: A connected realized informative graph is expected to identify the Rater block even without anchors, but minimal support may yield large condition numbers and finite-sample failures.
prospective_expectations_not_success_gat.hub_vs_chain: Equal nominal bridge counts need not have equal conditioning or recovery because edge topology and anchor location matter.
prospective_expectations_not_success_gat.rounding: No disagreement count is assumed; raw values remain authoritative regardless of the observed three/six-decimal audit.

interpretation_limits.ten_replicates: debugging evidence for design logic and failure modes, not confirmatory probability or precision
interpretation_limits.graph_prediction: a transparent topology rule to compare with exact rank, not a replacement for the exact conditional-information audit
interpretation_limits.anchor_share: randomized content reduces but does not eliminate finite ten-replicate content imbalance; no universal share is estimable
interpretation_limits.drift: not manipulated in this phase; differential drift distribution is the next separate registered phase
interpretation_limits.cross_engine: not addressed; later replay must respect each estimator's Person treatment and anchor contract
